title: Lake camps and Lincoln Beach
summary: Music was all along the lake's camps; Milton worked with Georgie Parker and notes musicians were scarce then.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: He was my Mama Lou's. He was at Mama Lou's. You know, he even passed there. He was my Mama Lou's. He was at Mama Lou's, yeah. When did Lincoln Beach start? He was more close, I mean, in town. Well, I worked at Happa Landon a long time too. I worked with Georgie Park out there a long time.
This was ten years ago. I heard music.
He was a Georgie Park piano player. Yeah. I worked with him a long time, I think.
I used to hear some music farther on, around the lake. Must be where Lincoln Beach is now. It was a long time ago, though.

Yeah, well, see, along them camps. They had music all over at that time. Every night, you see, that four or five camps had bands every night, but on weekends, most of every camp along that lake had bands. And then when you leave, well, Lincoln Beach is going to one little river all out there. They had picnics, you know, parties. Oh, man, music was good. Yeah.

Yeah. All you had to do is blow a horn a long time ago. You'd get work, I mean, because they didn't have that many musicians like they got now, you see. But all them little fellas now, they want to be musicians before they're long. They want to go play, you see. They didn't like that time before you had trouble. I mean, sometimes find musicians. But there's so many jobs, they ain't had enough musicians.
Some of them could play twice, but they play now.
